newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S TRC GRANTS TWO MORE AMNESTIES.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S TRC GRANTS TWO MORE AMNESTIES.

text.p: The Truth and Reconciliation Commission has granted two more amnesties for crimes committed for political reasons under apartheid.
But it said in a statement on Friday that it had refused one application and granted amnesties to two applicants only for one of the actions covered by their applications.
The latest batch of decisions by the commission headed by Archbishop Desmond Tutu follows hearings held in Potchefstoom last year.

Johnson Ncube and Mpayipheli Faltein, members of a self-defence unit at Khutsong, Carletonville, and of the African National Congress Youth League (ANCYL), had applied for amnesty for the murder of David Mayeko and the attempted murder of two othersin 1990.
Ncube was granted amnesty because the three victims were trying to inhibit ANCYL activities but Faltein was refused amnesty because he did not disclose all the relevant facts.

Mosiwa Popane, Dlanjiwa Gcinisizwe and Thamsanqa Mkontwana applied for amnesty for the killing of Nzimeni Mazwi and the attempted murder of Charles Mhlabiso in October 1990. Three three had been convicted of the charges and sentenced to between eight nd 12 years imprisonment.
The commision granted amnesty on both charges to Popane, who admitted taking part in the murder and stoning of the victim, but the other two only received amnesty for the attemtped murder charges.
